parts.title: Part 1 · Разговор по телефону
parts.intro: You will hear a woman joining a sports centre by phone. Complete the form. Write ONE WORD AND/OR A NUMBER for each answer.
script: Good morning, Riverside Sports Centre. How can I help?
Hi, I'd like to join the centre. I think I need to fill in a membership form.
Of course, I can do that with you over the phone. First, what's your surname?
It's Marlowe. That's M, A, R, L, O, W, E.
Thank you, Ms Marlowe. And your address?
My mobile is oh seven seven oh oh, nine oh one, three five eight.

Lovely. Now, we have two kinds of membership. Full membership is forty-two pounds a month and you can come at any time. Off-peak membership is only twenty-eight pounds a month, but you can only use the centre before four in the afternoon.
I work until five, so full membership would be better... actually, no. I work from home on Mondays, Wednesdays and Fridays, so I could come in the mornings. I'll take the off-peak one.
Good choice. And what do you mainly want to use the centre for? The gym, the classes, or the pool?
Mostly swimming. I might try the classes later.
Then you should come to an induction session. They're held on Thursdays at six o'clock in the evening.
Six is a bit late for me. Do you have anything earlier?
Let me check... there's one at half past five, the same day.
Thursday at half past five is perfect.
Great. Please bring some photo ID, like a passport, and a towel. There's also a deposit of five pounds for the locker key, which you get back when you leave.
You're welcome, Ms Marlowe. See you on Thursday.

«Mostly swimming».

6.00 ей не подходит, поэтому выбирают «half past five» — 5.30.
«Please bring some photo ID».

parts.title: Part 2 · Монолог (план здания)
parts.intro: You will hear a manager welcoming new volunteers to the Harbour Heritage Centre.
script: Welcome, everyone, and thank you for volunteering at the Harbour Heritage Centre. Let me start with a few practical points.

The centre opens to the public at ten o'clock. It used to open at half past nine, but we found that very few visitors arrived before ten. Volunteers, however, should arrive by nine thirty so that we can have a short briefing.
Parking is limited. Please don't use the visitors' car park at the front. Staff and volunteers park behind the building, and you reach it through the side gate on Mill Lane.
Everyone wears a name badge. Staff wear blue, and volunteers wear green, so visitors know who to ask for help. You'll collect your badge from reception each morning.

Our most popular exhibition is the model of the old shipyard. It's been here since the centre opened, and children love pressing the buttons to hear the sounds of the workers. The photography gallery is also good, but it's much quieter.

Now, let me tell you where everything is. Please look at the plan. When you come in through the main entrance, you'll see reception straight ahead. The cloakroom is just to your left as you enter, next to the door, so visitors can leave coats and bags there.

From reception, a long corridor runs straight ahead of you. On the left-hand side, the first door you come to is the cafe. The second door on the left, after the cafe, is the workshop room, where the weekend art classes are held. The room at the very top, at the far end of the corridor, is the lecture hall. You can't miss it.

Now the right-hand side. The toilets are at the bottom, near reception. Just beyond the toilets, the first door on the right, you'll find the first aid room. The next one, in the middle, is the library, and the room at the far end on the right, next to the lecture hall, is the quiet room. We keep it for visitors who need a rest.
Right, if you have any questions, please ask now. Otherwise, let's go and collect your badges.

parts.title: Part 3 · Обсуждение (студенты и преподаватель)
parts.intro: You will hear two students, Lena and Omar, discussing their project on food waste with their tutor, Dr Evans.
script: Come in, both of you. So, how is the food waste project going?
Quite well, Dr Evans. We've decided to focus on the university canteen rather than the whole campus.
That sounds sensible. Why the change?
At first we wanted to look at all the cafes, but we realised we wouldn't have enough time to collect the data. The canteen is the biggest, so it should give us enough information.
Good. And how will you collect it?
We'll weigh the leftovers at the end of each lunchtime for two weeks. We thought about asking students to fill in a survey, but people tend to say they waste less than they really do.
Quite right. Self-reported data is often unreliable. What about the results so far?
We only have the first three days, but the surprising thing is that most of the waste isn't food left on plates. It's the salad bar. People take too much and throw it away.
Interesting. Have you thought about what you'd recommend?
We're considering smaller plates at the salad bar. But Omar thinks that charging by weight would work better.
I do. Smaller plates just mean people go back more often.
Well, you don't need to decide yet. Now, let's talk about who does what. Lena, you're good with statistics.
Yes, I'll analyse the data, and I'll also do the slides for the presentation, since I've used that software before.
I'll design the weighing record sheets, and I'll write the final report. We'll both be at the canteen for the weighing, of course.
And the interviews with the canteen manager?
Yes, I emailed him last week. He's happy to talk to us next Tuesday.
Excellent. One last thing: please check your references carefully. Last year's group lost marks for that. The deadline is the fourteenth of December, and I'd like to see a draft a week before.

parts.title: Part 4 · Лекция
parts.intro: You will hear a lecturer talking about green roofs. Complete the notes. Write ONE WORD AND/OR A NUMBER for each answer.
script: Today I'd like to talk about green roofs, which are roofs covered with plants. They are not a new idea. People in Scandinavia were covering their houses with grass hundreds of years ago, to keep them warm in winter.

In modern cities, green roofs are valued for different reasons. First, temperature. On a hot summer day, a green roof can be up to five degrees cooler than a normal roof, and that helps to cool the whole street.
Second, water. A green roof can absorb up to seventy per cent of the rain that falls on it. This means less water pours into the drains during storms, so there is less flooding.

How is a green roof built? At the bottom, there's a waterproof membrane, which protects the building. On top of this goes a layer of soil, and finally the plants. For most roofs, the best choice is a plant called sedum, because it survives dry weather and needs almost no care.
One problem is weight. A green roof can weigh around one hundred kilograms per square metre, so the building must be strong enough. In older buildings, engineers have to check this first.

Another problem is cost. Installing a green roof costs about twice as much as a normal roof. However, it also lasts much longer. A normal roof may need replacing after twenty years, while a green roof can last for forty.
Finally, wildlife. Even small green roofs attract insects. In one study in London, researchers found several rare types of beetle on roofs that were less than ten years old.
As for cities that lead the way, Stuttgart in Germany has one of the highest numbers of green roofs in Europe. Some local councils there even pay part of the cost for homeowners.

items.why: «Around one hundred kilograms».

items.why: «About twice as much».

items.why: «Several rare types of beetle».
